policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'your zeal' renders the possessive alike whether the Greek reads the article with ὑμῶν or ὁ ἐξ ὑμῶν; 'the zeal from you' and 'your zeal' are not distinguished in the English, and the two notes here are an alternative rendering and a gloss on 'very many', neither mapped to this variant.
ASV's parenthesis reads 'that we say not, ye', a first person plural verb answering λέγωμεν; λέγω would have given 'that I say not'.

ASV ends the verse at 'in this confidence' with nothing for τῆς καυχήσεως; the longer reading would have produced 'this confident boasting' or 'this confidence of glorying', and ASV elsewhere renders καύχησις explicitly.

ASV 'go before unto you' renders either preposition with ὑμᾶς identically; εἰς and πρός are indistinguishable in this English, and the verse's two notes concern 'bounty' and 'extortion', not this unit.
ASV 'aforepromised bounty' renders a compound of ἐπαγγέλλομαι (promise); προκατηγγελμένην, from καταγγέλλω, would have given a prior announcing or notice rather than a promise.
ASV 'as he hath purposed in his heart' is a perfect, matching προῄρηται; the present προαιρεῖται would have given 'as he purposeth'.
ASV 'God is able' fits both the verb δυνατεῖ and the predicate adjective δυνατὸς with the copula; English supplies 'is' either way, so the wording does not distinguish them.
ASV 'seed to the sower' translates σπόρον and σπέρμα alike; both are rendered 'seed' and the English gives no feature separating them.
ASV reads 'shall supply', a future indicative statement, matching χορηγήσει; the aorist optative χορηγήσαι would have been rendered as a wish, 'may he supply'.
ASV 'shall supply and multiply your seed' carries the future indicative through to this verb, matching πληθυνεῖ rather than the optative πληθύναι ('may he multiply').
ASV 'and increase the fruits of your righteousness' continues the same future indicative construction, matching αὐξήσει; the optative αὐξήσαι would have given 'and may he increase'.

ASV 'Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift' has no connective, but ASV routinely leaves a transitional δέ unrendered, so the absence of 'Now' or 'But' does not settle whether δέ stood in the text.
